Xuan Kong Flying Star — venue mode, annotation, site model, worksheet

A walkthrough for App Review · bundle com.shenxuankong.app · version 1.0.0 (9) · English build

This page follows the app in the order a practitioner actually uses it: pick the kind of place (home / office / shop), take the facing, annotate the nine palaces with what is really there, model the site from measured numbers, read each annotated object, fold everything into one assessment, and print a worksheet. Nine screens, in that order, so each step can be checked in a few taps. The app opens in English via the “EN” pill at the top right.

What the app is

A measuring, annotating and reporting instrument for Xuan Kong Flying Star Feng Shui. Two inputs — a facing direction and a birth moment — plus whatever the user measures and places on site. From those it computes a nine-palace chart with documented arithmetic, keeps an indoor and an outdoor ledger that are never merged, models the surroundings in three dimensions, classifies each placed object against seven documented configurations with tolerance bands, and prints a ten-page worksheet. Everything is local; the cloud holds the account and, for subscribers, the sync.

Compared with the apps already in this category

The apps most often cited in this category each do one slice of the job. What follows is taken from their App Store descriptions as published; their engines are their own and are not judged here — the point is only to show where this app goes further.

What those apps coverWhat this app adds
Luopan / FengShui Transparent Compass — live 24-mountain compass, declination correction, overlay on floor plans and satellite maps, tap a palace for star meaningsThe facing is not the product, it is the first input: it selects the venue rule set, drives the site model and every verdict below (Fig. 1–5)
Feng Shui Compass: Luo Pan Kua — compass, personal Kua directions, yearly/monthly star references, saved projects with PDF reportsEight-mansions directions are one reading among several here; the app keeps two separate ledgers (indoor layout vs outdoor features) and reads each placed object against its palace (Fig. 5–7)
Karma Space (LiDAR) — scans the room with LiDAR, lays the nine palaces on the scanned plan, flags warningsA measured model rather than a scan: heights, distances, depth and rotation entered in metres, so an object’s angle relative to the house is a number the user controls (Fig. 6)
Feng Shui Hero / SpaceFlow — one photo or scan in, a single opaque score outEvery score is traceable to the measurement that produced it, with tolerance bands and a physical remedy per item — nothing opaque (Fig. 6–7)
House assumed; a workplace or a shop gets the same wordingThree venue modes with their own ledgers and wording — home, office, shop (Fig. 1–3)
Output is screen text or a screenshotA 10-page printable worksheet: verdict, per-direction actions, buy list, verification steps (Fig. 9)

Me → “Account” → Email → switch to the Password tab. The account already holds a saved chart and a completed survey, so every tab shows populated content on the first tap. No account is needed to look around.

Nine screens, in the order the app is used

Fig. 1 — Mode: home

A venue type is chosen once and then shapes the rest of the app: the indoor ledger switches to rooms (main bedroom, desk, stove, toilet) and the verdicts are worded for a dwelling.

The rule set is selected by venue type, not assumed.

Fig. 2 — Mode: office

Same chart, different ledger: the same nine palaces now take functions and fixtures of a workplace (workstation, reception, meeting room), and the verdict text changes with them.

One engine, three venue vocabularies — the switch is functional.

Fig. 3 — Mode: shop

The commercial ledger: counter, stock, entrance flow. The scores and the remedies follow the same nine-palace chart, read as a place of business.

A shop is not treated as a house with different labels.

Fig. 4 — Orientation feeds everything downstream

The facing is measured (magnetometer, declination-adjusted for 65 regions) or typed in. It is then carried into the chart, the site model and every verdict. The dial has three plate references (Earth / Heaven / Human) that change which ring the facing resolves against.

Orientation is an input the whole app depends on, not a readout.

Fig. 5 — Outdoor ledger: annotating the palaces

What is actually outside is placed on the nine palaces — a tower due Xu, a slope at the door, a river due Kan. The outdoor ledger is kept apart from the indoor one and the two are never merged.

The chart is annotated with real, placed features.

Fig. 6 — Sandbox: the site as measured blocks

The same features become a 3D model: heights, distances and angles taken from the ruler, your own building lit at its real floor. Below it, each feature listed with its measurement and the classification that follows (163 m / 194 m, 84 m / 194 m, -6 deg).

A model built from numbers the user measured — not an illustration.

Fig. 7 — Reading what was annotated

Every placed object is then read against its palace: what it governs, whether it presses on the house, and the remedy in physical terms (drain the earth, keep the door closed, add water). Change a measurement and the verdict changes with it.

The verdict is derived from the annotation, with a tolerance band and a remedy.

Fig. 8 — Whole-house assessment, and person-with-house

The parts are folded into one verdict: a score, what the house is like in this era, and the three moves that matter first. The card at the top is the joint reading — birth chart against house chart — for users who entered their four pillars.

The system converges to a single answer instead of leaving the user with nine pages.

Fig. 9 — The worksheet: 10 pages, printable

The assessment becomes a document: one overall verdict, what to do for each direction, what to buy, how to check the work. Saved to Photos and sent to a contractor or family member.

The output leaves the app — which is what makes it a tool.

Purchases

Two products through StoreKit: one subscription (monthly / quarterly / yearly, a single group, so switching a plan is a plan change rather than a second subscription) that unlocks the palace detail text and the whole-house assessment, and credit packs that unlock a single sheet. Price, period, auto-renewal and cancellation are stated on the purchase sheet; Restore Purchases is in the sheet footer and on the sign-in screen. No screen sends the user outside the App Store to pay.

In TestFlight the subscription banner reads “1 day left” for every period, because beta builds compress each period into one day. That is beta behaviour, not a defect.

Account and data

  • Sign-in is optional; a local profile works without an account.
  • Sign in with Apple and email + password are both supported.
  • Delete Account is inside the app and removes the cloud account, every profile, birth data and all saved work permanently.
  • Data collected: email, phone (only if the user picks phone sign-in), user ID, the birth details and site measurements the user types in, and purchase state. The privacy manifest declares no tracking.
Every screenshot is from build 1.0.0 (9), English build, iPhone 15 Pro, with a saved chart and a completed survey so that no screen is shown empty. Feature comparisons are drawn from the public App Store descriptions of the apps named, current at the time of writing.
